title: SmoothE: Differentiable E-Graph Extraction
problem: E-graph extraction—selecting the optimal expression from a compact equality-saturation graph—suffers from an unfavorable scalability-quality trade-off: exact methods are slow, and fast heuristics produce suboptimal results. Current methods also only support simple linear cost functions, limiting applicability to realistic optimization objectives (e.g., non-linear, learned cost models).
motivation: E-graphs are increasingly used in compilers, program synthesis, and theorem provers; extraction quality directly determines the quality of the optimized output, and existing extractors bottleneck the usefulness of equality saturation for complex real-world cost models.
method: SmoothE formulates e-graph extraction as a continuous, differentiable optimization problem by relaxing the discrete, combinatorial node-selection problem to a smooth objective over real-valued weights. Gradient-based optimization (e.g., gradient descent) is then applied to find the optimal extraction, enabling the use of arbitrary differentiable cost functions including learned neural cost models. The relaxation is designed so that the continuous optimum closely corresponds to a valid discrete extraction.
key_novelty: Reformulating e-graph extraction as a differentiable (smooth) continuous optimization problem, enabling gradient-based search and support for arbitrary differentiable cost functions beyond simple linear models.
contributions: SmoothE: a differentiable relaxation of the e-graph extraction problem to a continuous domain
Support for non-linear and learned (neural) cost models in e-graph extraction
Improved scalability-quality trade-off compared to existing exact and heuristic extractors
Applicability to compiler optimization, program synthesis, and theorem proving settings

metrics.other: improved scalability-quality trade-off over existing extractors; specific numbers not in abstract

baselines: existing e-graph extraction heuristics and exact solvers
limitations: The quality of the continuous relaxation's correspondence to valid discrete extractions under all cost models is not fully characterized in the abstract.
primary_theme: differentiable e-graph extraction for scalable compiler optimization
